mission.title: Long Distance
mission.description: Hijack a Network Media transceiver to hear the General's report from far beyond the Fields, and take it to the Merovingian.

npc.say:
It is strange to think of it, my friend: your entire world, blackened and dead, on and on, mile after mile... Quel dommage, eh? Such a waste...
Of course, I knew what had happened, but you like to think "ah, there must be something else that survived." But for the scout to travel 6000 miles, and see nothing but devastation... Zut alors!
But then, we are fortunate to have this place, non? The Machines who made it cannot be so bad, hm? Ah, well... We will see.

phase.briefing:
The General has been trying to contact us, operative, but his signal is so erratic that it's been difficult to track down.
Our technicians think they've managed to locate it at last. Hurry up and try to contact it.

enter.say:
Something tells me the General's getting himself into more trouble out there.
All right, that's the spot. I can see some kind of signal in there, but it's really weak.

done.say: Well great, I can't make anything out of that. What are we gonna tell Flood?

phase.briefing:
Why, why can't he simply get himself deleted? Is that so much to ask?
All right, operative. It's clear that the low-power transceiver we're using to communicate with the General without being detected by the Machines cannot handle communication at the range the General has reached in his pod-scouting venture. There's nothing for it but to upgrade temporarily, even though it may bring the wrath of the Machines down upon our--well, your--head.
Network Media runs the most powerful transceiver equipment in the city. We know that their CEO, the Network, does work for the Machines, and has equipment capable of communicating with them directly. I'm sure he won't mind if we repurpose one of his special communication arrays momentarily.

enter.say:
That's a Network Media broadcasting facility. You need to find a terminal that you can use to hijack their communication equipment.
I'm picking up some of their security team members in there, so keep an eye out.

done.say: An access key... That could come in handy.
Hm... Looks like a multi-part security access system there. You'll need two different access keys to get to the terminal we need.

objective.text: Use the Access Card on the security terminal

done.say: All right, now you just need a key for the other security terminal.

objective.text: Use the Access Code on the other security terminal

done.say: Nice. It looks like you can access the third terminal now.

objective.text: Hijack the communication equipment from the third terminal

done.say: That should have us plugged through his array now. I'm sure he won't mind too much; it's not like any of his subscribers watch TV over that one. He may miss out on some special chat time with Deus Ex Machina or whoever, but hey, these little inconveniences are what add spice to life, right?

phase.briefing:
Now hurry up and get to the General's signal again before they find out we've re-routed their equipment. We don't exactly want them listening in while the General airs their dirty laundry.
Hm... Then again, maybe we do.

enter.say: The General's broadcast signal is in there. Seems stronger this time; I hope that means its transmission is a little less garbled.

talk.say: One of my scouts followed the pattern of pod clusters to another collection of "Fields" over 6000 miles away. His signal ceased shortly thereafter, but it appeared to be roughly the same size as the other one, with a large pod cluster nearby. The power lines from the pod clusters had for some time been running the opposite direction: away from him. His report was the only ... to differ from the others; all scouts reported ... the surface area they scanned ... nothing but a ... featureless wasteland, its monotony relieved ... by dead skeletons of ... cities, Machine ... lines, and pod ...

done.say:
Broke up at the end there, but I got the part about finding another set of "Fields," anyway, and--
Oh! Watch it! Machine signals all over the place!

phase.briefing:
So the senile old fool wasn't just muttering incoherently after all, hm? What a novelty.
Very well, go report it to the Merovingian. If you're lucky, maybe Malphas will perform some more mathematical gymnastics for you.

enter.say: What do you suppose he meant about the power lines? If they weren't running to Machine city, then where were they going?

talk.say:
Hm... Another set of Fields... In that case, possibly there are several more that we have not discovered... That would account for the birth rate seen in the simulation, and it would fit with our estimate of 300 million total humans connected to the pods.
The General will have to be called back. We can't have him losing more Sentinels on long-range scouting--not if there is so little to see.

done.say: 300 million... They would all be taken up simulating just the United States of America of that time period. And yet, those in the simulation believe that they can travel anywhere in the world. Hm...

talk.say:
So! If it really is only 300 million that they have... Then I must say, mon ami, that I could almost feel sorry for them. You see, based on the power sample the General took, even 300 million would barely give them enough power to supply what we can guess of the energy demands of Machine city several times over...and out of that must also come power for their Sentinels, their other defenses, the Matrix itself...
It is a meager diet, I am afraid, and I see now why they harp so much on "efficiency." It explains why they have been less than overwhelming against Zion, eh? But it does not explain why it was not this way in the past... And it does not explain why they insist on using humans for power, when they must have much more enriching alternatives available.

mission.finish:
I'm sure I can't imagine why the Machines bother keeping you around, operative, unless they just like torturing you. But it certainly isn't making my job any easier.
And now they want to call the General back! Gad. Let him fly around your slush-pit of a world, I say. Anything's better than having him moping around here.
